source.title: Play fighting and the development of the social brain: The rat's tale.

confidence_rationale: Comparative-play anchor. Juvenile play deprivation in rats gives adults with socio-cognitive deficits and altered medial prefrontal neurons, and the benefit depends on keeping play reciprocal rather than on practising specific motor acts. This supports play as a developmental learning process and the social rung of ARC-136's ladder, but the mechanism described is reciprocity-regulated social calibration, not learning-progress-driven information hunger, so direction is mixed.
failure_signatures: The developmental benefit comes from the social coordination needed to keep play reciprocal, which an information-hunger drive does not specify; a learning-progress account alone would not predict that reciprocity is the critical ingredient.
Rough-and-tumble play is strongly motivated by its own reward system (opioid/endocannabinoid, 50-kHz calls) in rats; that looks like a dedicated play motivation, the thing ARC-136 says is not needed.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Depriving juvenile rats of peer-peer play leads to adult socio-cognitive deficits correlated with changes to medial prefrontal neurons; the benefit depends on using the abilities needed to keep play fighting reciprocal, so play fighting improves a general socio-cognitive skill set rather than training specific motor actions.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports two parts of ARC-136: play has real developmental consequences (it is not idle), and it trains general, transferable skill rather than specific acts, which fits an information/competence reading. It also populates the social rung of the claim's affordance ladder. It pushes against the claim's 'no dedicated play module' clause, because rodent social play has its own well-studied motivational machinery.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The claim explicitly disowns 'play = information gain' and allows bonding, practice and regulation, so a social-calibration function is not a contradiction; the tension is over whether a dedicated play motivation exists, which this review points toward for social play at least.
mapping.source_context: Review of the laboratory-rat play-fighting literature: behavioural development, play deprivation, prefrontal anatomy and physiology.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative review from the leading lab; mapping only partial because the proposed mechanism differs from the claim's.
